import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Unique realization of odd primes $p \notin \{3, 5\}$ by continued fraction values

$a(n)$ is the denominator of the finite continued fraction
$$\frac{1}{2 - \frac{3}{3 - \frac{4}{4 - \frac{5}{\dots - \frac{n-1}{(n-1) - \frac{n}{n+4}}}}}}$$

*References:*
- [A372761](https://oeis.org/A372761)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

namespace OeisA372761


open scoped Nat

open Rat

/--
Recursive helper computing the continued fraction denominator $R_k(n)$ for $2 \le k \le n-1$,
where $R_k(n) = k - \frac{k+1}{R_{k+1}(n)}$ with base case $R_{n-1}(n) = (n-1) - \frac{n}{n+4}$.
-/
def continuedFractionDenominator (n k : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  if n ≤ 2 then 0
  else
    if 2 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ n - 1 then
      if k = n - 1 then
        (k : ℚ) - (n : ℚ) / (n + 4 : ℚ)
      else
        let R_next := continuedFractionDenominator n (k + 1)
        if R_next = 0 then 0 else (k : ℚ) - (k + 1 : ℚ) / R_next
    else 0
termination_by n - k

/--
Denominator of the continued fraction
$$ \frac{1}{2 - \frac{3}{3 - \frac{4}{4 - \frac{5}{\dots - \frac{n-1}{(n-1) - \frac{n}{n+4}}}}}} $$
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n < 3 then 0 -- Sequence starts at n=3.
  else (1 / continuedFractionDenominator n 2).den


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 11 := by
  delta a; repeat rw [continuedFractionDenominator]; norm_num

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 4 := by
  delta a; repeat rw [continuedFractionDenominator]; norm_num

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_5 : a 5 = 7 := by
  delta a; repeat rw [continuedFractionDenominator]; norm_num

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_6 : a 6 = 13 := by
  delta a; repeat rw [continuedFractionDenominator]; norm_num

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_7 : a 7 = 31 := by
  delta a; repeat rw [continuedFractionDenominator]; norm_num


/--
Conjecture: Except for 3 and 5, all odd primes appear in the sequence once. - _Thomas Scheuerle_, May 11 2024

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/372761.wip.lean#L733"]
theorem exists_unique_a_eq_prime :
    ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p ∧ p % 2 = 1 ∧ p ≠ 3 ∧ p ≠ 5 → ∃! n, n ≥ 3 ∧ a n = p := by
    sorry

end OeisA372761

findings.description: The docstring attributes the conjecture to “Thomas Scheuerle, May 11 2024,” whereas the source literature attributes it to Mohammed Bouras. This is a provenance slip only: the Lean proposition faithfully states OEIS Conjecture 2.
findings.source_evidence: The official A372761 record credits Mohammed Bouras, May 12 2024, and contains the unsigned comment “Conjecture 2: Except for 3 and 5, all odd primes appear in the sequence once.” The paper linked by OEIS, Tom Adamczewski, arXiv:2608.11941v2, Appendix A, explicitly labels this exact claim “Conjecture (Mohammed Bouras, 2024).”
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the Scheuerle/date attribution with “OEIS A372761, Conjecture 2 (Mohammed Bouras, 2024),” or cite Conjecture 2 without a personal attribution.

reformulations.difference: The source gives an ordinary finite nested fraction. Lean totalizes its tails outside the valid index range and adds an explicit branch returning zero when the next tail is zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n ≥ 3 and 2 ≤ k ≤ n−1, backward induction gives R_k(n) > k(k−2)/(k−1) ≥ 0. The comparison values satisfy T_k = k − (k+1)/T_(k+1), and the terminal tail is strictly above T_(n−1). Thus every valid tail is positive and the zero guard is unreachable. The out-of-domain defaults likewise cannot affect indices n ≥ 3 in the theorem. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean I proved positivity, equality with the unguarded recursion, and the equivalence of the resulting conjecture statements, all without sorry or nonstandard axioms.

All 69 terms supplied by the OEIS b-file (n = 3 through 71) match Lean evaluation; the five test lemmas have clean axiom reports. The research-solved status agrees with OEIS's June 18, 2026 proof notice. The transferred theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
